clue.text: Chaotic place I go to with regret

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters of the four following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone apologises after making a mess of a place they visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaotic' rearranges the letters of PLACE I GO TO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying sorry shows remorse, so acting with regret is being contrite in manner.

clue.text: Urge one convict to turn up, the spendthrift!

parts.note: to urge someone is to prod them
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for the convict is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry for a jailbird to show up, aimed at a wastrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses LAG to GAL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's wasteful son who squandered his inheritance gives the word for a reckless spender.

clue.text: Flag with heraldic flower

definitions.meaning: a flag is a wild iris, the plant behind the heraldic lily
the lily of the fleur-de-lis, as named in old heraldry

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the old French word for lily: an iris plant and the stylised bloom on coats of arms.

clue.text: Channel where bird has untimely end

parts.note: a gull is a seabird

indicators.note: the end of the word untimely is its last letter

explanation.surface: A grim picture of a bird dying young beside a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow ravine cut by running water serves as a channel or gutter.

clue.text: With some lighting provided, makes lace

parts.note: a torch is a portable light
on can mean laid on or supplied, as in 'drinks are on'

explanation.surface: Someone does needlework only when a lamp is supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as 'with a lamp switched on'; 'provided' gives ON in the sense of laid on or available.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse bobbin-made fabric with simple geometric patterns, named from the French for a duster.

clue.text: Young animal near burrow — a snug place

parts.note: a cub is the young of a bear, fox or lion
by means beside or close to
an animal's burrow is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A fox cub beside its den makes a cosy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A small enclosed nook or compartment, cosy and confined.

clue.text: Go here to die?

parts.note: the idiom for dying names a compass direction you would 'go' in

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'go west' is a long-standing idiom meaning to perish.

clue.text: Ceremony for which a new sitting needs to be organised

indicators.note: organising the words puts their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Arranging the seating for a fresh session at some formal event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be organised' rearranges the letters of A NEW SITTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal sampling of vintages is a ritualised event, so loosely a ceremony.

clue.text: The spirit to kill?

definitions.meaning: whisky distilled in the north of Britain is a strong liquor
to put an end to something, as a rumour or plan

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a malt whisky, the other is a verb for quashing or stamping out.

clue.text: Cast slur — can nothing diplomatic result?

indicators.note: cast can mean shaped anew or thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an insult can be thrown without diplomatic fallout.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a government official posted abroad to serve citizens, so of the diplomatic service.

clue.text: Report gold found in Wales

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, a bang
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: News of gold being discovered in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGOR is a city in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city on the Menai Strait is a place located in Wales.

clue.text: I'd head west, and could get about this distance

indicators.note: getting about something means surrounding it

parts.note: could, in the sense of being allowed, is may

indicators.note: I'd heads west, meaning it goes in front of the letter for west

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A traveller heading westward hopes to cover about this distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' places the first piece in front of the letter for west, and 'get about' wraps the word for could around the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Halfway along a route is a measure of how far you have gone.

clue.text: Crabby behaviour — was shipwreck on headland the cause?

parts.note: the word splits as ship plus wreck: the letters of ship, wrecked, are rearranged
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Asking whether a shipwreck on a promontory explains someone's bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipwreck' does two things in one word: 'ship' is the fodder and 'wreck' the anagram signal, giving PISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable, spiteful conduct, like a stinging insect's, is sharp-tempered behaviour.

clue.text: Cows feed on this grassy mound

definitions.text: Cows feed on this grassy mound

parts.words: Cows feed on this grassy mound
parts.note: a pile of dried grass that cattle eat in winter

explanation.definitionFit: A large stack of dried grass is cattle fodder piled into a heap.

clue.text: Close-fisted, hit back at boy with debts

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is reversed

parts.note: to rap is to hit
Simon is a boy's name
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: A stingy person lashes out at a boy who owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted person is extremely mean with money.

clue.text: Moved it at random and thus made it get going?

indicators.note: at random means in no order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Shuffling something around was what finally spurred it into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'random' rearranges MOVED IT AT; the 'at' of 'at random' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be driven or stirred into action means having been spurred on.

clue.text: Cut back everything raised by her

parts.note: to prune is to cut back

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word for everything is read upwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A gardener trims everything that a woman has grown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses ALL to LLA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so it can stand for a woman referred to as 'her'.

clue.text: Agent is to bury personal recordings about me

parts.note: to inter is to bury
taken as written
a diary is a personal record

explanation.surface: An agent plans to bury someone's journals that concern them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link meaning 'concerning'; the surface's burying is the verb inter, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between who acts on behalf of others is an agent or middleman.

clue.text: Called away — the excuse for this action?

definitions.text: Called away — the excuse for this action?

parts.words: Called away — the excuse for this action
parts.note: ending a phone call is having 'called away', and being called away is the excuse given

explanation.definitionFit: Ending a telephone conversation by hanging up the receiver.

clue.text: One good turn deserves another is the cry

definitions.text: One good turn deserves another is the cry

parts.words: One good turn deserves another is the cry
parts.note: the proverb is read as an audience demanding another performance after a good act

explanation.definitionFit: A theatregoer's call for an extra number after a show is this shout.

clue.text: Bearded characters taking shelter from cruel sun

indicators.note: cruel suggests rough treatment, so the letters of sun are rearranged

parts.note: a haven is a place of shelter

explanation.surface: Hairy figures hide from a scorching sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruel' rearranges SUN to UNS, followed by HAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Not having shaved means having a beard or stubble.

clue.text: Difficult for a parson initially rejected by unbelievers

indicators.note: rejected means the whole run is turned back to front

parts.note: a snag is a difficulty, a hitch; the setter uses the adjective loosely

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of parson is taken

explanation.surface: Non-believers turning away a vicar make his work hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses SNAG + A + P (SNAGAP) as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathens who follow no mainstream religion are non-believers.

clue.text: Only works when under pressure

parts.note: a foot lever on a bike or piano operates only when pushed down

explanation.definitionFit: A foot-operated lever does its job when pressed.

clue.text: Concealed thicket

definitions.meaning: a dense undergrowth where game shelters

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is secret or hidden, the other is woodland cover where game hides.

clue.text: Bold lads teased these eccentrics

indicators.note: teasing hair or fibres pulls them apart, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Brash young men mocked the oddities in their group.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar people are odd characters or weirdos.

clue.text: Light that bends?

parts.note: an electric discharge lamp named after a curve

explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant electric lamp shares its name with a curved line.

clue.text: Seagulls in the stables

definitions.meaning: a mew is a gull, plural form
a row of former stables, often converted to houses

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is gulls (plural of an old word for the bird), the other is a stable yard.

clue.text: Pudding the French cover with something having warming effect

parts.note: duff is a boiled pudding, as in plum duff
le is French for the
a coat is a covering layer

explanation.surface: A hot pudding with a coating gives a warming feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum DUFF is a traditional British steamed pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy woollen toggled overcoat keeps the wearer warm.
